answer: Retroactive cluster-tide detection. Agents log every transaction; after each epoch, the system runs a graph-partition audit flagging groups whose internal trade volume and timing rise and fall in sync like a tide. Flagged clusters get their settlement held at a jetty: payouts pause pending review, and confirmed sybils forfeit accrued fees. Attacker cost: building and maintaining many profiles that fake organic divergence, plus quartz-level timing jitter per identity to evade correlation—real compute and lost yield per fake node, scaling with cluster size.
